To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CCL21, in conjunction with CCL19, regulates the anatomical distribution of splenic MZ macrophage in the steady state.
CCL21 plays a significant role in the localization of MZ macro-phages within the splenic marginal zone.

1) MZM localize to the splenic marginal zone in response to chemokines CCL19 and, to a greater extent, CCL21; 2) MZM are selectively lost from the MZ during infection with the parasite Leishmania donovanii; and 3) this loss is mediated in part by the absence of CCL19/CCL21 in the spleen of L. donovanii-infected mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of chemokine receptors in the localization of MZ macro-phages.
how the immune system recognizes and responds to pathogens.
the role of C-C chemokine ligand 21 in the maintenance of marginal zone macrophages in the steady state and during infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CCL21 is the key chemokine for the localization of MZ macrohages in the marginal zone.
CCL19 and/or CCL21 are required for the localization of MZ macrohages within the marginal zone of the spleen.
C-C chemokines are important for MZM localization and that pertussis toxin is an inhibitor of chemotactic responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CCR7 ligands CCL21 and CCL19 play a role in the localization of MZ macrohages in the spleen.
the chemokines CCL19 and, to a greater extent, CCL21 play a significant role in the maintenance of the MZM in the spleen, and that this is likely to be mediated by the chemokine receptor CCR7.
CCL19 and, to a greater extent, CCL21 play significant roles in maintaining the distinctive anatomical location of MZM in the spleen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCL21, and CCL19 to a lesser extent play a significant role in maintaining the anatomical localization of MZ macrohages in the spleen of uninfected mice.
CCL19 and, to a greater extent, CCL21 play a critical role in maintaining the localization of MZ macro-phages within the MZ.
the chemokine receptor CCR7 plays a critical role in maintaining the localization of MZ macro-phages (MZM).
